headline: 15,000+ passengers affected as 103 Dhaka-Saudi flights cancelled
summary: Flight suspensions follow Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, including Riyadh and Dammam, causing widespread travel disruptions.
details: Over 15,000 passengers have been affected after 103 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia were cancelled or suspended. According to Shahjalal International Airport authorities, this includes 41 direct flights and 59 transit flights.

Among the direct flights, Biman Bangladesh Airlines cancelled 17, US-Bangla Airlines 10, Saudia Airlines 7, and Riyadh Airways 7. US-Bangla has suspended flights to Riyadh until October 21, while Biman has suspended flights to Dammam and Riyadh until October 17.
Transit disruptions were led by IndiGo Airlines with 22 cancellations, followed by Emirates (14), Salam Air (7), Qatar Airways (7), Fly Dubai (6), Air India (2), and Egypt Air (1).

The cancellations follow a series of Houthi attacks on Riyadh and Dammam airports in Saudi Arabia. A recent attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 13 people, including two Bangladeshis, and injured 308 others, including 27 Bangladeshis.

The Iran-backed Houthi group has vowed to continue attacks on airports and oil installations, including a previous attack on Saudi Aramco headquarters. They claim these sites are legitimate targets in retaliation for Saudi intervention in Yemen.
Aviation experts express concern that the escalating conflict in the Persian Gulf could lead to further widespread disruptions to international air traffic.

headline: Tk 30,000 basic salary demand: Garment workers block Uttara highway
summary: Protesters blockaded the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for the fourth day, bringing traffic to a standstill before police intervened.
details: Garment workers from several factories in Uttara have blockaded the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for the fourth consecutive day.
The protesters are demanding a minimum basic salary of Tk 30,000 and other benefits to cope with the rising cost of living.
The blockade brought traffic to a complete standstill for nearly two hours, causing significant disruption to commuters.
Police used batons and sound grenades to disperse the crowd and clear the highway.
The protests have persisted as workers seek a wage hike to match current economic pressures.
